result.summary: Replaces manual parameter extraction, null checking, and fallback default handling across node and wallet RPC endpoints with the `self.Arg<T>(name)` helper. It updates `GetParamIndex` to match the primary argument name using `GetFirstName()` when parameter aliases exist, adds template instantiations for `double` and `int64_t`, and converts `verifychain` metadata to use `RPCArg::Default`.
result.problem: RPC endpoints frequently duplicate parameter logic by checking `request.params` index validity and hardcoding fallback defaults that are already declared in the method definition metadata. This boilerplate creates redundant code and risks drift between documented defaults and actual execution.
evidence: PR description: 'The `Arg()` helper has many benefits: It does not require manual `isNull` checks, It does not require hard-coding the fallback/default value a second time, It does not require manually specifying the getter for the type. Specifying the type is enough.'
result.scope_notes: Touches 14 RPC and wallet RPC source files mechanically replacing `request.params` index access with named `self.Arg` lookups.
result.changed_since_previous: Includes a minor documentation typo fix in a comment in walletcreatefundedpsbt.
result.card: Replaces manual RPC parameter null-checking and fallback logic across node and wallet RPC commands with the self.Arg<T>(name) helper. This removes boilerplate and prevents re-declaring parameter default values that are already defined in the RPC metadata. It also updates GetParamIndex to resolve parameter aliases via their primary name and adds missing type instantiations. The change is an internal refactoring with no stated change in user-facing behavior.

risk.why: A typo in an argument name or a subtle difference in type conversion or default resolution could alter RPC behavior or cause crashes on unexpected inputs across multiple wallet and node RPC endpoints.
